classes.name: Oral corticosteroids
classes.description: Systemic oral corticosteroids: prednisone (tablets, solution; Rayos delayed-release appears discontinued), methylprednisolone (Medrol, dose pack), prednisolone (solution, Orapred ODT, Millipred), dexamethasone (tablets, solution, Dexamethasone Intensol, TaperDex/Dxevo/HiDex packs; Hemady 20 mg is labeled for multiple myeloma only, an alternative, never the pick), hydrocortisone (Cortef; Alkindi Sprinkle and Khindivi oral solution for children). Deflazacort (Emflaza) and vamorolone (Agamree) for Duchenne are specialty alternatives only, never the pick. Not budesonide (Entocort, Uceris, Tarpeyo) or inhaled/topical steroids.
classes.plainDescription: Short courses of steroid pills that calm inflammation fast, for flares of asthma, COPD, arthritis, allergies and more.
classes.indication: Inflammatory flares, asthma/COPD exacerbations, autoimmune disease, adrenal insufficiency

preferredAgent.sig: Dose by condition, 5 to 60 mg by mouth daily, with food (label). A common short course for a flare is 40 mg once daily for 5 days (practice, not label text); taper courses longer than 2 to 3 weeks.
preferredAgent.sigShort: 5-60 mg QD; flare often 40 mg x5d
preferredAgent.plainSig: Take with food in the morning, at the dose and for the days your prescriber sets.

records.verificationNote: Not a PDL class: the PDL legend says any therapeutic class not listed "will continue to be covered" for DC Medicaid fee-for-service members (p. 6). Coverage and restrictions for this class are not in the document; absence from the PDL is not treated as exclusion. The PDL has no systemic oral corticosteroid class: the only corticosteroid classes are ophthalmic, intranasal, inhaled and topical (pp. 58, 63-64, 67-68). Prednisone, methylprednisolone, prednisolone, dexamethasone oral, hydrocortisone (Cortef, Alkindi, Khindivi), Rayos, Hemady, Emflaza and Agamree are not printed. The sig is a label-style placeholder by indication; the PDL prints none. [Sonnet check 2026-11-24: sig changed to a real label regimen with course length; absence re-confirmed by page-text grep of all 70 pages.]

records.verificationNote: Read pp.30-31 (adrenal and corticosteroid lines): prednisone, methylprednisolone and prednisolone tier '1, 2, 3'; hydrocortisone '1, 3, 4'; dexamethasone '1, 2, 3'. Tier is split by form, so the tablet's tier is not confirmed. No restriction printed on any oral steroid. SOLU-CORTEF (tier 2, 3, MB, p.31) and CELESTONE SOLUSPAN (p.30) are injectables under the medical benefit; left out. Rayos, the Medrol brand, TaperDex/Dxevo/HiDex packs and Millipred/Orapred are not separately printed; the generic lines are read as covering the generic products. The Rayos brand is not on the list and is multi-source by prednisone name, so not recorded as nonformulary. [Sonnet check 2026-11-21: tier cell lists several tiers with no form printed on the list (p.2 says tiers can differ by dosage form), so the exact form's tier cannot be read; stays partial. No PA/ST/QL flag on the line, confirmed.]
